headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the full cost of their dedicated grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Governor Abigail Spanberger, consumer advocacy groups, Piedmont Environmental Council.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines.
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must cover the full cost of transmission infrastructure built to serve their operations, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers. This decision, supported by Governor Abigail Spanberger, is projected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to enhance transparency and aid in water supply planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia.
news_summary: New regulations taking effect in January will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to provide more transparency. This bill, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Delegate Joshua Thomas, Governor Spanberger.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law.
news_summary: Virginia's new law, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct site assessments, including noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, and exempts expansions under 100 megawatts.
